issue.description:
Observed 2026-10-17 in ~/utilities: on 2026-09-29 a worker hand-edited the root object objects/98541406….jsonl, blanking 3 records, so the file no longer hashed to its name. bead sync status then reported 'root hash mismatch … Ready to commit: NO' for 18 days. bead sync flush-only published a new generation, gen-0a345ea5, whose pointer still named the same root, because the live state was unchanged and so the content address was identical. The corrupted file was trusted by name and never rewritten, so publication could not repair the checkpoint. It took a real mutation (new content, new name) to produce a verified root.

Expected: when the target object path already exists, verify its sha256 against the name before reusing it. On a mismatch, rewrite it atomically from the live serialization, or fail the publication loudly. Either way, a flush on an aligned store must leave both pointers referencing verified objects.

Acceptance: a test plants a byte-modified object at the exact content address the next publication would use. flush-only then either rewrites it, so sync status shows the root as verified, or exits non-zero naming the object. It must never report success while the root is unverified. Context: utilities repair util-efe25b30; root cause of the edit, secret-scanner fss-4adff6a8 / fss-2e0b117e.
issue.notes: Implemented verify-before-reuse at both checkpoint object write sites (commit bf2aa10b): the monolithic root publisher and write_content_object each sha256-verify an existing object before reusing it and atomically rewrite it from the live serialization on mismatch, naming the repair on stderr and listing the repaired path in changed_paths. Acceptance replayed by tests/checkpoint_object_reuse_verification.rs: a corrupt object planted at the recomputed address is repaired by flush-only and status then reports root_verified=true with the mismatch reason gone; healthy reuse of a verified root is pinned byte-for-byte. Verified in a git-archive extraction of HEAD (/var/tmp/dod-fb3100ce-hNqX): definition-of-done --fast exit 0 (140 suite result lines, no failures), acceptance test target exit 0 with a fresh bead-rs Compiling line, clippy --all-targets -D warnings exit 0. Pushed bf2aa10b to origin/main; rev-list origin/main..HEAD empty.
issue.title: Checkpoint publication reuses an existing content-addressed object without verifying its bytes

issue.description:
Auto-split child 1/4 of beadrs-5d781dc7 (umbrella: make archive-build regression tests pass outside a VCS checkout).

Scope: the environment classifier in tests/build_from_archive_checkout_untouched.rs that decides whether VCS-state assertions apply at all.

- Distinguish a real checkout (.git present) from an exported tree (git-archive extraction, unpacked package).
- Refuse to classify as exported on .git absence alone: if git still resolves a work tree from that directory, FAIL loudly instead of skipping (a destroyed .git, or a tree nested inside an enclosing repo, must not silently inherit the skip).
- Emit a loud, self-describing skip message for genuine exported trees, naming the environment and what is being skipped.
- Give the classifier its own unit-level coverage: real checkout -> full assertions; exported -> loud skip; disagreement -> failure.

Acceptance:
- Classifier tests pass.
- A real checkout is never classified as an exported tree.
- Disagreement between .git absence and git's work-tree resolution is a failure, never a skip and never a pass.
issue.title: Classify checkout context before asserting VCS state
